MCP connector

# Pinterest keyword data inside ChatGPT and Claude

Ask your assistant how competitive a Pinterest keyword is, what ranks for it and what is rising, and it answers from pins we actually measured. **15 lookups a month free**, and a keyword we do not hold costs nothing.

## The quick way: sign in, no key to copy

Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code can connect with just the server URL. They open a PinPinterest sign-in, you press Allow, and the app gets its own key (it shows in **Settings → API** as “connected”; revoke it there to disconnect).

### Claude.ai & Claude Desktop

Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.

Name it PinPinterest, paste https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp and leave the OAuth fields empty.

Press Connect, sign in to PinPinterest (or create your account) and press Allow.

### ChatGPT (developer mode)

Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings → turn on Developer mode.

Create a connector with https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp and choose OAuth as the authentication.

Sign in to PinPinterest in the window it opens and press Allow.

### Claude Code

Run this once, then type /mcp in Claude Code, pick pinpinterest and choose Authenticate.

Sign in to PinPinterest in the browser tab it opens and press Allow.

```
claude mcp add --transport http pinpinterest https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp
```

### Cursor & VS Code

Add the server with only its URL, https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp (no headers).

Press the sign-in button the app shows beside it, sign in to PinPinterest and press Allow.

Server URL: `https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp`. An app that cannot sign in (n8n, a script) uses a key, below.

## 1. Get your API key

Create an account, then open **Settings → API** in the dashboard and press Create key. The same key works for the [REST API](https://pinpinterest.com/developers) and here, and both draw on one monthly allowance.

Server URL: `https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp`

## The pin limit

Each plan can see a set number of **different** pins in any 30 days, with a tenth of it a day. One count covers the API, the MCP and the app together. A pin counts once per 30 days, so re-reading pins you have already seen is free, and keyword numbers (searches, related terms, trends) are not part of it.

- **Starter**: 20,000 different pins a month, 2,000 a day
- **Pro**: 60,000 different pins a month, 6,000 a day
- **Studio**: 200,000 different pins a month, 20,000 a day
- **API Scale**: 350,000 different pins a month, 35,000 a day

At the limit, pins you have already seen still come back and new ones pause: the API answers HTTP 429 with `code: "pin_limit"`, `returns_at` (when new pins return) and `upgrade_plan`; a page that only partly fits answers 200 with the pins that fit and a `pin_limit` object. Why a pin limit? It keeps the data fair and fresh for everyone and stops bulk copying of the database.

## 2. Add it to your app

### Claude Code

Run this once in your terminal, then ask Claude Code a Pinterest question.

```
claude mcp add --transport http pinpinterest https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer pp_live_YOUR_KEY_HERE"
```

### Claude.ai & Claude Desktop

Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.

Name it PinPinterest and paste this URL (with your key in place of the placeholder). Leave the OAuth fields empty.

```
https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp?key=pp_live_YOUR_KEY_HERE
```

### ChatGPT (developer mode)

Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings → turn on Developer mode.

Create a connector, paste this URL (with your key), and choose "No authentication" — the key in the URL is the authentication.

```
https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp?key=pp_live_YOUR_KEY_HERE
```

### Cursor

Add this to the file, then reload Cursor.

File: `~/.cursor/mcp.json`

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pinpinterest": {
      "url": "https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer pp_live_YOUR_KEY_HERE"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code (Copilot agent mode)

Add this to the file in your workspace, then start the server from the file.

File: `.vscode/mcp.json`

```
{
  "servers": {
    "pinpinterest": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer pp_live_YOUR_KEY_HERE"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### n8n

Add an MCP Client Tool node to your AI Agent and fill in these three fields.

```
Endpoint: https://api.pinpinterest.com/mcp
Server Transport: HTTP Streamable
Authentication: Bearer Auth → pp_live_YOUR_KEY_HERE
```

Replace `pp_live_YOUR_KEY_HERE` with your key. Keep a URL with your key in it private — anyone holding it can spend your lookups. You can revoke a key and make a new one at any time.

## 3. Ask

- How competitive is "fall porch decor" on Pinterest, and is it worth a pin?
- Those dog-grooming keywords came back as not tracked — ask PinPinterest to crawl all of them.
- Give me ten related Pinterest keywords for "meal prep" with low competition.
- Show me the top pins ranking for "capsule wardrobe" and what their titles have in common.
- Which Amazon and Etsy products do people save most for "small kitchen organization" on Pinterest?
- What are the most-saved video pins in home decor from the last 30 days?
- What is rising in the food niche right now?
- How many PinPinterest lookups do I have left this month?

## The tools

| Tool | What it answers |
|---|---|
| `keyword_lookup` | Pinterest data for one keyword: how many ranking pins we analysed, their average and total saves, competition (low/medium/high) and an opportunity score, plus its niche. est_clicks is an ESTIMATE derived from saves (Pinterest does not publish clicks or impressions for pins you do not own); pins_analysed, saves and competition are measured from the pins we crawled. On Pro and above: demand is our high/medium/low word from average saves (the word the app shows); google_monthly_searches is GOOGLE's average monthly US searches for the exact term, never Pinterest's — Pinterest publishes no monthly search counts. Today it is null for every keyword: the Google feed it comes from is switched off and not being refreshed, so do not plan around it. pinterest_search_count is Pinterest's own search count for the exact phrase, from its public interest page (read at pinterest_search_count_at; Pinterest does not say what period it covers, so use it to compare phrases, never as searches per month); null when Pinterest has no interest for the phrase. A keyword we do not hold returns tracked:false with close suggestions and does not use a lookup. Its crawl field says what happens next: on a paid plan we have already started crawling it (crawl.status queued or crawling) — tell the person to ask again in crawl.retry_after_minutes, or that we e-mail them when it is in. When several keywords come back tracked:false, offer request_keywords to queue them all in one call. |
| `request_keywords` | Ask PinPinterest to crawl Pinterest for keywords it has no data for yet — offer this after keyword_lookup answers tracked:false, especially for a list. Pass up to 25 terms; each comes back with a request_id and a status (queued, crawling, ready, failed). Crawls usually land within 10–40 minutes and the person gets ONE e-mail when they are in; asking keyword_lookup again after crawl.retry_after_minutes returns the data. Asking twice for the same term is the same request. Uses no lookup; up to 25 new keywords a day per account. Needs the Starter plan or above. |
| `related_keywords` | Keywords that appear on the same ranking pins as yours, strongest overlap first — the ones worth targeting next. Each comes with how many pins it shares and its own competition. Needs the Starter plan or above. |
| `keyword_top_pins` | The best-performing pins ranking for a keyword, by saves, with their titles, links and save counts — what is winning that search right now. est_clicks is an ESTIMATE derived from saves (Pinterest does not publish clicks or impressions for pins you do not own); pins_analysed, saves and competition are measured from the pins we crawled. Needs the Pro plan or above. |
| `top_products` | The products that win a keyword on Pinterest: its most-saved pins that link to a shop (Amazon, Etsy, Walmart, Target and more), grouped by product, with each product's pins, total saves, newest pin and how fast it is rising. No prices: pins do not carry them. est_clicks is an ESTIMATE derived from saves (Pinterest does not publish clicks or impressions for pins you do not own); pins_analysed, saves and competition are measured from the pins we crawled. Needs the Pro plan or above. |
| `niche_top_pins` | The best-performing pins across a whole niche (use list_niches for the slugs), sorted and paged. Pass next_cursor back as cursor for the next page. There is no impressions sort: Pinterest does not publish impressions for pins you do not own, so we do not invent them. Needs the Pro plan or above. |
| `trending` | Topics rising in a niche right now, read from the pins people are publishing this month, with example pins. Use list_niches for the slugs. |
| `list_niches` | The niche slugs the other tools accept (niche_top_pins, trending). Free — uses no lookup. |
| `my_quota` | Your PinPinterest plan, how many lookups you have used this month and when they reset. Free — uses no lookup. |

Each tool is a REST endpoint underneath, with the same numbers, the same plan rules and the same meter — see the [allowance on each plan](https://pinpinterest.com/pricing#api). When the month runs out, the assistant tells you, along with the plan that lifts the limit.

A keyword we have not crawled yet costs nothing. On a paid plan we start crawling it the moment you ask, and `request_keywords` queues a whole list in one go — you get one e-mail when they are in, and asking your assistant again then answers with the data. [How the crawl works](https://pinpinterest.com/developers#crawl).

## Get a key

Create an account, open Settings → API, press Create key. The free allowance never expires.
